core_thesis: NVIDIA remains positioned to capture a large share of enterprise and hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending because its compute, networking, software, and developer ecosystem remain tightly integrated and difficult to displace in the near term.
key_assumptions: AI training and inference demand continues to grow across hyperscalers and enterprise customers.
NVIDIA maintains performance and ecosystem advantages that support premium pricing.
Customers continue to view accelerated computing as a high-priority capital allocation area.
Supply availability improves enough to support shipment growth without a major deterioration in customer relationships.
Export restrictions and competitive responses slow some regions or products but do not fully offset broader demand growth.
upside_drivers: Faster-than-expected inference demand broadens the customer base beyond a small set of hyperscalers.
New product ramps increase system-level revenue through combined GPU, networking, and software sales.
Enterprise adoption shortens the path from pilot workloads to production deployments.
Gross margin remains resilient despite mix shifts as software and platform attach rates increase.
downside_risks: Hyperscaler capital spending becomes more cyclical or more concentrated in fewer customers.
Tighter export controls reduce addressable demand or create product segmentation challenges.
Competition from internal silicon or rival accelerators pressures pricing, share, or workload mix.
Supply chain or packaging constraints delay shipments and compress near-term revenue conversion.
Margin pressure emerges if product transitions or regional mix changes dilute the current economics.
macro_sensitivities: Cost of capital and duration-sensitive equity valuation
Global growth and enterprise IT spending conditions

core_thesis: Coca-Cola remains positioned as a defensive consumer staples business because its brand portfolio, global distribution system, and pricing power help support resilient cash generation across a wide range of macro environments.
key_assumptions: Consumers continue to treat core beverage categories as repeat-purchase products even in slower growth environments.
Coca-Cola maintains brand strength and route-to-market advantages that support pricing actions without a severe erosion in demand.
The company continues to balance pricing, mix, and packaging decisions in a way that protects margins over time.
Global distribution and franchise execution remain strong enough to support broad market coverage across regions and channels.
FX volatility and input cost inflation create pressure at times but do not fully overwhelm the defensive quality of the business.
upside_drivers: Pricing power remains durable while consumer demand stays stable across key markets.
Volume trends improve as execution, channel mix, or international recovery supports broader consumption.
Margin stability holds as management offsets input cost pressure through mix, pricing, and operating discipline.
The stock retains defensive appeal if investors rotate toward cash-generative and dividend-oriented businesses.
downside_risks: Input cost inflation compresses margins if pricing actions lag cost pressure.
FX headwinds weigh on reported results or reduce the benefit of underlying operating performance.
Volume growth weakens if consumers trade down, reduce discretionary purchases, or face sustained macro pressure.
Execution or channel disruptions limit the benefit of the company's global distribution footprint.
Defensive quality becomes less valuable to investors if growth-sensitive assets re-rate more strongly.
macro_sensitivities: Global growth and emerging market demand conditions
metrics_to_monitor: Gross margin and operating margin stability
